The Global Obidient Movement has condemned the alleged intimidation of market women in Benin City, Edo State, over their support for the National Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, warning that no Nigerian should be victimised for supporting a political leader. The movement’s National Coordinator, Dr Moses Paul, stated this in a statement on Friday, following reports that some traders around Ring Road in Benin City were allegedly being forced to shut their shops and trading spaces after welcoming Obi during his recent visit to the state. Paul described the reported treatment of the traders as unacceptable, insisting that no citizen should be punished for exercising their constitutional rights. “No woman should lose her means of livelihood because she welcomed a political leader. No trader should be intimidated for expressing a political preference. No citizen should be punished for exercising a constitutional right,” he said. He demanded the immediate restoration of the affected women’s trading spaces and called for an end to what he described as intimidation, harassment and victimisation, regardless of those responsible. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Our politics must never become a weapon against the poor. The market woman who sells to feed her children deserves the same freedom, dignity and protection as the most powerful politician in this country,” Paul said. He also expressed pride in the reception accorded Obi during his visit to Edo State, saying the turnout demonstrated that the Obidient movement remained strong in the state. According to him, the large turnout, hours spent on the streets and sacrifices made by supporters were not ordinary political displays but expressions of their conviction and belief in a better Nigeria. They came to welcome, celebrate and identify with a man whose politics represents their aspirations for a country that works for everyone,” he said. Paul urged supporters in Edo State not to be discouraged by the reported incidents, but to remain peaceful, disciplined and focused. “To the Obidients in Edo State: Do not be discouraged. Your enthusiasm must translate into organisation, your passion into responsibility, and your numbers into votes. We must remain peaceful, disciplined and focused,” he added. He maintained that the movement was committed to a Nigeria where citizens could freely express their political preferences without intimidation. The statement comes days after gunmen attacked supporters of the NDC along Airport Road in Benin City during Obi’s visit to the state, leaving one person with gunshot injuries. The Edo State Police Command confirmed the November 25 incident, saying three gunmen in a black Toyota Hilux opened fire on people at the scene after encountering police operatives stationed at the airport exit gate. The police said the victim, identified as Aimionkhale Micheal, sustained injuries to his thighs and was receiving medical attention. The command also said it had launched an investigation to apprehend the fleeing suspects. Christabel Ndoeche
